methodology: Generated capability/consumer mapping; statuses do not imply production effectiveness. Wired means a callable implementation; partial means scope or delivery gaps; missing means no end-to-end consumer; external requires independent evidence. Includes proposed market capabilities and deployment/assurance requirements. Historical module-reachability counts are not feature counts.

features.name: Tool artifact extraction
features.delivered: Commands, paths, URLs, package specs and content; unknown and MCP tool input is walked to depth 16, 1024 strings, 2048 artifacts and 4 MiB, object keys are inspected, free text over 64 KiB (including Write/Edit/Read content) is scanned in overlapping line-aligned windows, and any residual limit marks the call input_not_fully_inspected, which the evaluator denies (POL-INPUT-003) instead of allowing it uninspected
features.remaining: Unrecognized or host-hidden actions remain outside visibility; an oversized benign tool input is now denied rather than allowed, so the limits still need calibration against customer workloads

features.name: Prompt injection inspection
features.delivered: Bounded pre-model tool-result inspection in OpenCode, VS Code, SDK and OpenClaw (tool-result middleware on the embedded runner); Claude Code replaces the result through PostToolUse updatedToolOutput and Cursor uses host-specific later boundaries. Real-host records (linux/x64, development build, scripted mock model) show a secret-bearing tool result reaching the model only as AIDR's quarantine notice on Claude Code 2.1.282, OpenCode 1.18.32 and the OpenClaw 2026.9.6 embedded runner, and post-tool-output is sold for those three connectors (OpenClaw since 2026-09-30). Sensitive-output quarantine now fires only on high-precision findings (verified key/token formats, PEM key material, Luhn cards, labelled SSNs), so timestamps, hashes, UUIDs and git emails no longer quarantine output
features.remaining: The real-host records quarantine one secret-bearing Bash/exec result with a scripted model; prompt-injection payloads, MCP and non-text results, Cursor/VS Code and Codex (no output interception) are not host-accepted, and OpenClaw's pre-model quarantine covers only the explicitly enabled plugin on the embedded runner (not the Codex harness); provider streams and native host bypass need acceptance; the precision filter trades recall on unlabelled formats and needs customer benign/attack corpus calibration

features.name: Prompt protection and DLP input redaction
features.consumer: UserPromptSubmit (Claude Code, Codex, VS Code), beforeSubmitPrompt (Cursor), chat.message (OpenCode), before_agent_run (OpenClaw) and connectors that declare input rewrite
features.delivered: Prompts are scanned for secrets (block by default), PII including TC Kimlik, IBAN and TR/international phones from the AIDR Privacy rules (warn by default) and tenant DLP, with kinds/counts only. Overlap resolution is a linear sort-and-sweep, a blocking scan stops at the first confirmed secret, and an internal deadline (default 7 s; the host kills the hook at 10 s) blocks an unfinished scan when secrets=block or a tenant DLP policy applies and otherwise sends the prompt with a visible not-fully-inspected notice; an incomplete personal-data scan is never reported clean. A DLP redact becomes an allow with rewritten input only where the host supports rewrite (Claude Code updatedInput, OpenCode args), using shell-inert REDACTED tokens, only if every parameter survives and the rewritten input rescans clean against DLP and the threat heuristics (dlp_redaction_unsafe otherwise); everything else is denied. Real-host records (linux/x64, development build, scripted mock model) show a prompt carrying a GitHub token never reaching the model on Claude Code 2.1.282, Codex CLI 0.141.0, OpenCode 1.18.32 and the OpenClaw 2026.9.6 embedded runner; pre-prompt is in the sold support matrix for those four connectors since 2026-09-30
features.remaining: The four records cover linux/x64, a development build and a scripted mock model only (no Windows/macOS/arm64, signed artefact or real model); the Cursor and VS Code prompt hooks have no real-host record and are not sold as enforced; a Codex prompt hook that is untrusted, crashed or timed out, and a Claude Code or VS Code hook killed before it answers, let the prompt through (host behaviour); OpenClaw's gate runs in the embedded and CLI runners only; Codex, Cursor, VS Code and OpenClaw keep redact as deny; with PII in the default warn mode a prompt that could not be fully inspected is still sent with a notice; the rewrite contract is verified locally against one Claude Code version and still needs native host-version acceptance

features.name: Session toxic-flow and behavioral chain detection
features.consumer: Evaluator per tool call, fed by the connector post-tool/output handlers
features.delivered: Per-session capability tracking of private-data access, untrusted content and external communication (the lethal trifecta); the call that would complete a dangerous chain is flagged with the chain steps named, taint follows downloaded files by path; session records are HMAC-bound so a tampered record is treated as having all three capabilities, and unreadable state is recorded as toxic_flow_unavailable, never as clean
features.remaining: Classification is heuristic and one level deep (bash -c, eval, argv, common prefixes); a custom binary that uploads data is not recognised as external communication, taint does not cross agent sessions or follow a moved/renamed download, and false-positive rates on real agent sessions are unmeasured

features.name: Data and context poisoning protection
features.consumer: Evaluator write/read paths, MCP gateway tool lists and package installs
features.delivered: 23 CTX rules: write-time review of instruction, memory, agent-settings and MCP configuration files (a benign edit asks), read-time poisoned-context findings in tool output, hidden-Unicode detection, MCP tool-description poisoning and rug-pull checks through the gateway and signed manifests, memory/RAG write poisoning, and slopsquatting checks on young or unknown packages
features.remaining: Pattern-based: a paraphrased instruction without a covered signal is caught only by the path-based review; shell writes built at run time are not attributed; tool descriptions are visible only through the MCP gateway or signed manifests; Codex has no read-time layer and enforces ask as deny; PyPI adoption uses release count because it has no download API

features.name: Canary credentials (honeytokens)
features.consumer: aidr canary deploy/list/remove/status, evaluator and output inspection, incidents page
features.delivered: Six decoy kinds (AWS, GitHub, OpenAI, .env, SSH config, database URL) planted by an operator-only CLI with a digest-only registry; opening, searching or sending a decoy value is denied and recorded as a high-severity canary_triggered incident; an agent running aidr canary is blocked (CLT-CANARY-001); an unreadable registry is reported as canary_unavailable, never as clean
features.remaining: A split, reversed or encrypted value is not recognised (base64 only from the start of the run); directory-wide reads that do not name a decoy are caught only in the tool output; relative paths match by trailing segments; Browser Guard treats decoys as ordinary secrets

features.name: Agent-safety guardrails for autonomous agents
features.consumer: Shared evaluator for every connector and the MCP gateway, local mode
features.delivered: 43 rules and a session runaway guard: loops, repeated failures, rate spikes and optional budgets pause the session (ask); diff-aware reward-hacking checks (skipped tests, removed assertions, bypassed hooks, disabled CI, lowered coverage, blanket suppressions, force-push to protected branches) ask; launching an agent with approvals or sandbox off is denied; irreversible actions (drops, teardown, deletions, publishing, production deploys, payments) ask with an Irreversible action label
features.remaining: Shell rules see the command line, not what a script it runs does; diff-aware checks read the previous file from disk (regular files up to 1 MiB); a force-push without a branch name cannot be tied to a protected branch; repeated-failure detection depends on the host reporting failures; efficacy on real agent sessions is unmeasured

features.name: AI model supply-chain and secure-code guardrails
features.consumer: Evaluator on commands and agent-written code, connector warnings
features.delivered: 14 AISC rules for unsafe model loading (pickle/torch.load without weights_only, trust_remote_code, unsafe Keras/numpy/YAML loaders) and untrusted model downloads with a trusted-publisher list, and 27 secure-code rules that warn on TLS-verification bypass, eval of untrusted input, SQL and command injection and over-broad file permissions in code an agent writes
features.remaining: Pattern rules over the written text: no cross-file data flow or renamed imports, model files themselves are not inspected, and the secure-code findings are advisory warnings, not a static-analysis or secure-code certification

features.name: Prompt jailbreak and content-safety policy

features.delivered: Jailbreak categories (instruction override including Turkish phrasings, persona override, constraint release, many-shot framing, encoded payloads) and content-safety categories, each block, warn or off (jailbreak defaults to warn), provisioned per tenant through a prompt_safety block; findings name the category only
features.remaining: Phrase and pattern based, not a moderation model; the default is warn rather than block, a connector build that predates the prompt_safety field rejects a provisioned payload carrying it (and fails closed), so connectors must be upgraded first, and false-positive/evasion rates on customer prompts are unmeasured

features.name: Out-of-band operator approvals and operator CLI
features.consumer: aidr pending/approve/allowlist/audit/doctor and guardToolCall in OpenClaw, OpenCode and Codex
features.delivered: HMAC-signed pending asks and single-use, tool- and artifact-bound approvals (15-minute default expiry) in a 0600 store. The HMAC key lives only in the OS vault by default: with no vault, approvals are disabled and asks stay blocked, and a plain key file needs an explicit key_storage=file that aidr doctor warns about. Single use is anchored in a vault-held consumption ledger, so restoring an old approvals.json yields already_used. Self-defense hard blocks CLT-SELF-007/008/009 deny any agent reference to the state directory, the vault entries or aidr approve/pending/allowlist add over a shell-normalised view (quotes, escapes, ANSI-C strings, variables, concatenation, globs). Stored and displayed records escape C0/C1, bidi and format controls with a truncation marker and artifact count. Interactive TTY confirmation or explicit non-interactive opt-in; no agent-callable approval tool
features.remaining: Approval is local to one host and OS user: there is no central/multi-approver workflow. The agent runs as the same OS user, so separation rests on the OS vault's own access policy and on pattern-based self-defense rules, not on process isolation; a shell construct the normaliser does not model, or a vault that releases secrets to any process of the user without a prompt, can still expose the channel. Real macOS/Windows/Linux vault behaviour, operator usability and native host acceptance remain open

Never agent-callable

features.name: Agent permission profiles
features.consumer: Evaluator for every connector and the MCP gateway, aidr profile, Policies page templates and staged profile editor, operator provisioning script
features.delivered: Least-privilege profiles per connector and repository (tool classes, command prefixes, file paths, domains, MCP servers/tools, default action) merged with detection as deny > ask > allow; a profile never relaxes a threat verdict, allowlists do not lift it, profile ask is operator-approved out of band and profile deny cannot be approved; local and signed managed profiles with templates. Owners and administrators (AAL2) validate profile documents in the dashboard with the engine schema (a generated, drift-checked Edge copy) and stage versioned, audited revisions with diff and rollback, through four-eyes change control when it is on; scripts/provision-agent-profiles.mjs pulls the tenant's current staged revision, checks its recorded sha256, re-validates it and signs it into the tenant detector bundle with the operator key. Repository-scoped profiles also apply to calls that name an absolute or ~/ path inside the repository, added to the working-directory selection
features.remaining: Command prefixes are coarse (a program an allowed prefix starts can do anything it does); shell words are checked lexically against files.deny; repository selection sees the host-reported working directory and absolute paths a call names, not paths reached indirectly; a staged profile is not enforced until an operator signs it into the bundle (the control plane holds no key connectors trust for detector policy and delivers no bundle)
